title: Card Sharp
summary: Tap cards to count a reduced sample space for P(A | B), then set chances for independent events and for draws without replacement.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Conditional probability in a reduced sample space
At least one, by the complement
learningOutcome: The student can find P(A | B) by counting in the reduced sample space, use P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B) for independent events, and find chances for draws without replacement.

levels.title: The reduced deck
levels.adds: Baseline: given B, the sample space is the outcomes of B, and P(A | B) = n(A ∩ B)/n(B) (Ex 13.1 Q6 to Q15; Examples 2 to 5).
hints: First mark only the cards that fit B: the sample space shrinks to them.
Then mark again the cards that also fit A.
The chance is the green cards out of all the marked cards.

levels.title: Independent events
levels.adds: New: A and B are independent when P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B), which gives the unknown chance by division (Ex 13.2 Q1, Q4 to Q8; Examples 10 to 13).
hints: Write P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B) with the known values.
Divide P(A ∩ B) by P(A) to find P(B).
Write P(B) in twelfths to read k.

levels.title: Without replacement
levels.adds: New: P(both red) = (r/N)((r − 1)/(N − 1)), and P(at least one) = 1 − P(none) (Ex 13.2 Q2, Q3, Q12 to Q14; Examples 8, 9).
hints: After the first card is drawn, the deck has one card fewer.
For at least one, take 1 minus the chance that both are black.

levels.title: Not and or
levels.adds: New: P(E′ | F) = 1 − P(E | F) and P(A ∪ C | F) = P(A | F) + P(C | F) − P(A ∩ C | F), counted on the reduced deck (Section 13.2.1).
hints: First mark every card that fits B: that is the new sample space.
Not A: the cards of B that do not fit A.
A or C: count A and C, and do not count the overlap twice.

misconceptions: P(A | B) is the same as P(B | A)
Count all the cards, not just those in B
Draws without replacement keep the same chance each time
